result.keywords:
Abstract
                Background
                Optimizing clinical workflows in hospital information systems requires accurate handling of Chinese clinical text and robust technical assessment methods. This study proposed a hybrid attention-based neural framework to evaluate and improve workflow support within HIS environments.
              
                Methods
                We combined a CNN-LSTM-CRF style information extraction module with a Delphi-informed checklist for assessing communication service, system architecture, security service and response time. The model was applied to a set of inpatient and outpatient records from a tertiary hospital.
              
                Results
                The proposed approach identified workflow bottlenecks and improved extraction accuracy for key clinical entities. Evaluation scores were strongest for security service and response time, while communication service and system architecture showed moderate gains.
              
                Conclusions
                An integrated neural and technical evaluation framework may support more reliable HIS deployment and clinical text processing in Chinese hospitals.
